title: AI Unlocked: Finance & Accounting
blurb: For accountants, analysts, and finance teams: close-and-reporting acceleration, Excel/Sheets AI mastery, FP&A and analysis workflows, the finance-AI tool market compared, and the controls/audit-trail discipline regulators expect.

modules.d: Where AI creates value across the finance cycle — and why numbers demand stricter discipline than words.
modules.body:
Finance is a special case for AI

Language models are probabilistic: they predict plausible text. That is excellent for drafting, explaining and summarising, but dangerous for arithmetic and facts presented as certain. A sentence that is slightly wrong is a nuisance; a reconciliation that is slightly wrong can mislead a board, misstate tax or hide a fraud. Finance professionals who succeed with AI therefore adopt one governing principle: use AI to build, explain and check the work — let deterministic systems (spreadsheets, accounting software, code) do the calculation — and verify everything that leaves the team.

Mapping AI across the finance cycle

  • Transaction processing: extracting data from invoices and receipts, suggesting account codes, matching payments to invoices. Increasingly built into accounting platforms; still requires review of exceptions.
  • Record-to-report and month-end close: drafting reconciliation checklists, investigating variances, writing journal descriptions, and preparing close commentary.
  • Spreadsheets and analysis: writing and explaining formulas, cleaning data, building pivot tables and models faster.
  • FP&A: driver-based forecasts, scenario analysis, and the narrative explaining performance.
  • Reporting: management packs, board commentary, and summaries tailored to different audiences.
  • Audit and controls: testing populations of transactions for anomalies, documenting controls, and drafting policies.
  • Tax and compliance: summarising regulations and preparing questions for advisers — but tax positions require qualified review and authoritative sources.
The calculation boundary. Ask AI "Write an Excel formula that calculates the variance between actual and budget for each cost centre" — not "What is the variance between these numbers?". The first produces a transparent, auditable formula in a deterministic tool; the second produces an answer you must re-check by hand.

The changing role of finance professionals

As routine processing is automated, finance teams spend relatively more time on analysis, business partnering, controls and judgement. The skills that grow in value: understanding the business drivers behind numbers, communicating insight to non-finance leaders, designing controls for automated processes, and evaluating whether AI-produced work is right. A finance professional who cannot explain why a number moved is more exposed than one who cannot type a formula.

Risks specific to finance

  • Calculation errors presented confidently, especially with long tables pasted into chat tools.
  • Confidentiality: unpublished results, payroll, client financial data and price-sensitive information entered into tools without appropriate data protection — potentially a breach of law, contract or market rules.
  • Outdated or wrong rules: AI may describe accounting standards or tax rates incorrectly or from an earlier version.
  • Weakened audit trail: numbers that cannot be traced to source data and logic fail audit.
  • Automation bias: reviewers approving AI-prepared work too quickly because it looks professional.

A maturity view

Finance teams typically move from ad hoc individual use, to standardised prompts and templates with review rules, to embedded AI features in accounting and FP&A systems with documented controls, to optimised processes where close cycles, forecasting and reporting are redesigned around automation. Each step requires stronger controls, not weaker ones.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as a finance transformation advisor. Ask me about my role, team size, accounting software, close timeline and biggest time sinks. Map AI opportunities across our finance cycle, rate each for value and risk, and recommend three starting use cases. For each, specify where the calculation must happen in a deterministic tool and what review control is required.

📚 Glossary

  • Deterministic tool: software that gives the same exact result from the same inputs, e.g. a spreadsheet formula
  • Record-to-report: the process from recording transactions to producing financial statements
  • FP&A: financial planning and analysis
  • Automation bias: over-trusting automated outputs
  • Audit trail: traceable path from reported figures back to source data and logic

📖 References

  • ICAEW — Generative AI guidance for accountants.
  • ACCA — Reports on AI and the accountancy profession.
  • IFAC — Technology and the future of the profession resources.

quiz.q: Aminata, an analyst at a Douala distributor, has 400 transaction rows and needs totals by department for tomorrow's management pack. Which approach best fits the course's governing principle?
opts: Ask the assistant for the totals twice in separate chats and use them if both answers agree
Paste the rows in smaller batches of 50 so the assistant is less likely to make arithmetic slips
Ask the assistant to write a SUMIFS or pivot setup, then compute the totals in the spreadsheet
Paste the 400 rows into the chat, ask for the totals, then spot-check two departments by hand
quiz.x: The calculation belongs in a deterministic tool; AI builds the formula. Spot-checking two departments (runner-up) still relies on a probabilistic tool for arithmetic and leaves most totals unverified.

quiz.q: A Nairobi NGO's finance officer is choosing a first AI use case. Which task carries the lowest risk while still saving real time each month?
opts: Drafting plain-language commentary on variances the officer has already calculated and reconciled
Asking the assistant which withholding tax rate applies to a new consultancy contract this year
Having the assistant suggest and post journal corrections where the trial balance looks unusual
Letting the assistant compute monthly grant burn rates from a pasted extract of the general ledger
quiz.x: Drafting on top of verified numbers keeps calculation and judgement outside the model. Computing burn rates (runner-up) looks harmless but puts arithmetic inside a probabilistic tool.

quiz.q: A regional manager in Abidjan signs off an AI-prepared management pack after a quick read because the charts and wording look polished. Two figures later prove wrong. Which risk materialised?
opts: Weakened audit trail on the figures
Automation bias by the reviewer
Outdated rules in the AI's training
Confidentiality breach of the pack
quiz.x: Over-trusting work because it looks professional is automation bias. A weakened audit trail (runner-up) concerns traceability to source, which the scenario does not describe.

quiz.q: An AI assistant tells a Yaoundé accountant the standard VAT rate in Cameroon and drafts an invoice template using it. What is the most appropriate next step before the template goes live?
opts: Use the template but add a note asking customers to report any tax rate they think is wrong
Ask the assistant to cite its source for the rate and accept it if a plausible law is quoted
Compare the rate with last year's invoices and adopt it if the two figures happen to match
Confirm the rate against the current finance law or a tax adviser and record the source used
quiz.x: Tax rules change and AI may cite earlier versions, so verification against an authoritative current source is needed. Matching last year's invoices (runner-up) misses any change in this year's finance law.

quiz.q: A Lagos bank is redesigning finance roles as invoice processing becomes automated. Which capability should it prioritise developing in its accountants over the next two years?
opts: Typing complex nested formulas quickly from memory without lookup or assistance
Processing a higher daily volume of invoices manually as a backup to automation
Memorising the current year's tax rates so staff can answer questions instantly
Explaining the business drivers behind movements and judging if AI output is right
quiz.x: The lesson says value shifts to analysis, business partnering and evaluating AI work. Formula fluency (runner-up) still matters but is exactly what AI increasingly accelerates.

quiz.q: Two days before results are published, the CFO of a listed Johannesburg retailer wants to paste the draft results into a free consumer chatbot to draft the press release. What is the main concern?
opts: Consumer chatbots tend to produce text that is too long for a standard results announcement
The chatbot may produce a press release in a tone that the investor relations team dislikes
Unpublished price-sensitive data would enter a tool lacking agreed data protection terms
The draft may contain arithmetic errors that the chatbot would copy into the press release
quiz.x: Entering price-sensitive, unpublished information into an unprotected tool risks breaches of law, contract and market rules. Arithmetic errors (runner-up) are a real risk but secondary to the disclosure exposure.

quiz.q: External auditors at a Kampala manufacturer ask how a forecast revenue figure was derived. The analyst can only say it came from an AI chat last month. Which finance-specific risk does this illustrate?
opts: Model drift over time
Weakened audit trail
Automation bias by staff
Outdated accounting rules
quiz.x: A figure that cannot be traced to source data and logic fails audit — a weakened audit trail. Automation bias (runner-up) may have contributed but describes reviewer behaviour, not traceability.

quiz.q: A Ghanaian finance team has moved from each person using AI ad hoc to shared prompt templates and written review rules, but no AI is yet embedded in its accounting system. Which maturity stage is it at?
opts: Standardised
Ad hoc use
Optimised
Embedded AI
quiz.x: Shared prompts, templates and review rules define the standardised stage. Embedded (runner-up) requires AI features inside accounting or FP&A systems, which the team has not yet adopted.

quiz.q: A controller in Kigali needs gross margin % for 300 product lines. Revenue is in column C and cost of sales in column D. Which prompt best respects the calculation boundary?
opts: Write a formula for column E giving gross margin % from C and D, handling zero revenue
Here are C and D for all 300 lines; calculate gross margin % and return it as a table
Explain gross margin % and then estimate the average margin across these 300 product lines
Calculate gross margin % for the first 20 lines so I can copy the pattern for the others
quiz.x: Asking for a transparent formula keeps the arithmetic in the spreadsheet. Calculating 20 lines (runner-up) still asks the model to do arithmetic and gives nothing auditable to extend.

quiz.q: A US mid-market company switches on AI auto-categorisation and bank matching in its cloud accounting system. What should happen to its finance controls as a result?
opts: Move review to year-end, when auditors will test the automated categorisation anyway
Reduce manual review gradually as the auto-categorisation accuracy rate improves
Keep them as they are, since vendor-built features have been tested by the supplier
Document and strengthen them for the automated steps, including exception review
quiz.x: The lesson stresses that each maturity step needs stronger, documented controls. Reducing review as accuracy improves (runner-up) sounds efficient but removes the oversight that catches residual errors.

facts.t: Language models predict plausible text — they do not calculate deterministically.
facts.more: Use AI to build, explain and check the work; let spreadsheets, accounting software or code do the arithmetic.

facts.t: OHADA member states, including Cameroon, sharing uniform business and accounting law.
facts.more: Their entities apply SYSCOHADA — a key test when judging whether a foreign finance AI tool fits.

facts.t: Fixed number of CFA francs (XAF) per euro.
facts.more: The peg has held since the euro's launch in 1999. AI tools sometimes 'convert' with a live rate; check which rate a model assumes.

facts.t: Finance AI maturity: ad hoc → standardised → embedded → optimised.
facts.more: Each step needs stronger controls, not weaker ones.

steps.s: An analyst wants the chatbot to compute variances for 40 cost centres from a pasted table.
o: Ask AI for a variance formula and run it in Excel
Transparent, auditable, deterministic.
Let AI compute, then spot-check three lines
Better than nothing, but errors hide in unchecked lines.

Untraceable numbers presented confidently.

steps.s: The draft commentary is excellent, but one line says 'margin rose because of lower fuel costs'.
o: Keep it; it sounds plausible and fits the trend
Plausible isn't evidence; causes must be verified.
Check with operations whether fuel costs fell
Verify drivers before they reach the board.
Delete all causal explanations from the report to be safe

steps.s: The CEO asks you to paste unpublished results into a free AI tool to make slides.

Protects confidential, price-sensitive information.
Agree, since it is internal use

modules.d: Formulas, data cleaning, modelling and verification in Excel and Google Sheets — with AI as your expert pair.
modules.body:
The spreadsheet remains the finance professional's main instrument

Despite enterprise systems, most analysis, reconciliation and modelling still happens in Excel or Google Sheets. AI dramatically accelerates spreadsheet work: writing formulas you would otherwise search for, explaining inherited models, cleaning messy exports and building structures. The professional's job is to specify precisely and test rigorously.

Prompting for formulas

A good formula prompt states: the spreadsheet application and version (Excel 365 and Google Sheets differ), the sheet and column layout with sample values, the exact logic required, edge cases (blanks, zeros, errors, duplicates), and the output location. Example: "In Excel 365, Sheet 'Sales' has Date in A, Region in B, Product in C, Amount in D (rows 2–5000). On Sheet 'Summary', B1 is a region and B2 a month (first day of month). Write a formula returning total Amount for that region and month, returning 0 if none." A correct answer would use SUMIFS with date bounds such as EOMONTH.

The functions every finance user should command

  • Lookup: XLOOKUP (Excel 365 and Google Sheets) replaces VLOOKUP's fragility — it searches any direction and handles not-found values. INDEX/MATCH remains essential for older files.
  • Conditional aggregation: SUMIFS, COUNTIFS, AVERAGEIFS, MAXIFS.
  • Dynamic arrays: FILTER, SORT, UNIQUE, SEQUENCE — producing ranges that update automatically.
  • Readability: LET names intermediate calculations inside a formula; LAMBDA creates reusable custom functions in Excel.
  • Error handling: IFERROR and IFNA — use carefully; hiding all errors can conceal real problems.
  • Dates: EOMONTH, EDATE, NETWORKDAYS, YEARFRAC.

Cleaning data with AI help

Exports from banks, payroll and ERPs arrive with inconsistent dates, text-numbers, trailing spaces, merged headers and duplicates. AI can write formulas (TRIM, VALUE, TEXTSPLIT, DATEVALUE) or step-by-step Power Query transformations, which are repeatable every month — far better than manual cleaning. For recurring imports, ask AI to design the Power Query steps once and refresh monthly.

Test every formula like an auditor. ① Check it against three to five rows you calculate by hand, including an edge case. ② Reconcile totals to a control figure (the ledger, bank statement or source total). ③ Use Excel's Evaluate Formula or trace precedents to follow the logic. ④ Ask the AI to explain the formula line by line — if the explanation does not match your intent, the formula is wrong.

Understanding inherited models

Finance teams inherit complex workbooks with hard-coded numbers and undocumented logic. Paste a formula (not confidential data) and ask AI to explain it in plain language and identify risks: hard-coded constants, inconsistent ranges, circular references, or lookups that will break if rows are added. This turns days of reverse-engineering into hours.

Modelling standards

Good financial models separate inputs (clearly marked assumptions), calculations and outputs; avoid hard-coded numbers inside formulas; use consistent formulas across rows; include checks (balance sheet balances, totals reconcile) that flag errors visibly; and document sources. AI can audit a model structure against these standards and draft a model documentation sheet.

Built-in spreadsheet AI

Microsoft Copilot in Excel and Gemini in Google Sheets can analyse tables, suggest formulas, create charts and summarise data within the file. Availability and capabilities vary by licence and change frequently. Use them for speed, but apply the same tests: built-in does not mean verified.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my spreadsheet expert. I will describe my sheet layout with sample (non-confidential) values and the result I need. Write the formula for my exact application (Excel 365 or Google Sheets), explain it line by line, list edge cases it handles and does not handle, and give me three test rows with expected results. If a repeatable cleaning task is involved, propose Power Query steps instead.

📚 Glossary

  • XLOOKUP: flexible lookup function replacing VLOOKUP/HLOOKUP
  • SUMIFS: sums values meeting multiple criteria
  • Dynamic array: formula returning a range that resizes automatically
  • LET / LAMBDA: naming intermediate values / creating custom functions
  • Power Query: repeatable data import and transformation tool
  • Control figure: an independent total used to reconcile results

📖 References

  • Microsoft Support — Excel function reference and Copilot in Excel.
  • Google — Google Sheets function list and Gemini in Sheets.
  • ICAEW — Financial Modelling Code.
  • FAST Standard — financial modelling guidelines.

quiz.q: A SUMIFS formula written by AI for a Douala distributor returns regional sales that differ from the general ledger control total by 2,350,000 FCFA. What should the analyst do first?
opts: Accept the formula total because the ledger may contain postings that are still unapproved
Test sample rows by hand and check the criteria ranges and date bounds against the ledger
Ask the AI to rewrite the formula with XLOOKUP and see whether the difference disappears
Post the difference to a suspense account so the pack can go out and investigate next month
quiz.x: A mismatch to the control figure signals a formula or data issue to investigate by hand-testing and checking ranges. Rewriting with another function (runner-up) changes the formula without diagnosing the cause.

quiz.q: An analyst at a Texas retailer needs monthly sales by region on a Summary sheet. Which prompt is most likely to produce a correct formula first time?
opts: Write me a robust formula that totals sales by region and month on my summary sheet, with error handling
In Excel, sum the Amount column for the region in B1 for the month in B2 using whatever function is best
Excel 365: Sales!A2:D5000 holds Date, Region, Product, Amount; B1 is region, B2 month start; return 0 if none
Give me three alternative formulas for a regional monthly sales total so I can choose the one that works
quiz.x: A good prompt names the application, layout, logic, edge case and output. The runner-up prompt (sum the Amount for B1 and B2) omits the sheet layout and the not-found behaviour.

quiz.q: A Ugandan analyst wraps every lookup in a 50-sheet model in IFERROR(…, 0) so the outputs look clean for the board. What is the main risk?
opts: The workbook will recalculate noticeably more slowly once the model grows past 50 sheets
IFERROR does not work in Google Sheets, so the model cannot be shared with the auditors
Board members may assume the zeros are forecasts rather than actual reported figures
Genuine errors such as missing supplier codes appear as zeros and understate totals
quiz.x: The lesson warns that hiding all errors can conceal real problems — missing lookups silently become zero. Slower recalculation (runner-up) is a minor performance point, not a reporting risk.

quiz.q: Every month a Cameroonian microfinance institution receives the same bank export with text-numbers, trailing spaces and merged headers. Which approach is best?
opts: Ask AI each month to write fresh TRIM and VALUE formulas for the new file
Use AI to design Power Query steps once, then refresh the query each month
Clean the file by hand each month using a checklist drafted by the AI
Paste the export into AI monthly and ask it to return a cleaned version
quiz.x: Power Query makes the cleaning repeatable and auditable. Monthly TRIM/VALUE formulas (runner-up) work but are rebuilt each time, inviting inconsistency.

quiz.q: A VLOOKUP in an Accra company's cost model returns wrong values after a colleague inserts a column in the lookup table. Which change most reduces the chance of this recurring?
opts: Replace it with XLOOKUP referencing the return column
Add IFERROR so broken lookups return a blank cell
Lock the lookup sheet so nobody can insert columns
Convert the lookup table into a named fixed range
quiz.x: XLOOKUP references the return column directly, so inserted columns do not shift results. Protecting the sheet (runner-up) prevents the trigger but blocks legitimate maintenance and leaves the fragile design.

quiz.q: Copilot suggests a formula for a Kenyan company's cash forecast. Which verification routine best matches the course's audit-style testing?
opts: Ask Copilot to explain the formula and accept it if the explanation sounds reasonable
Compare the result with last month's forecast and accept it if the change looks small
Hand-check three to five rows including an edge case and reconcile totals to the bank
Have a second AI tool write its own formula and accept the result if both of them agree
quiz.x: Hand-testing rows with an edge case plus reconciling to a control figure is the course's routine. A plain-language explanation (runner-up) is one step of it, but on its own does not test the numbers.

quiz.q: A Senegalese model has '*1.18' typed inside dozens of formulas to apply a tax rate. Which modelling standard is breached, and what is the fix?
opts: Consistent formulas across rows: copy one master formula down each column
Visible checks: add a cell that flags whenever totals fail to reconcile
Documented sources: add a comment citing the finance law for the 18 %
Inputs separate from calculations: move 1.18 to a labelled input cell
quiz.x: Hard-coded constants breach the inputs/calculations separation; one labelled input cell fixes every formula when the rate changes. Documenting the source (runner-up) helps but leaves the rate buried in dozens of formulas.

quiz.q: A new controller in Lomé inherits a workbook with a 400-character nested formula and no documentation. What is the best use of AI here?
opts: Paste the formula, without client data, and ask for a plain-language explanation and risks
Ask the AI to rebuild the entire model from scratch following current modelling standards
Ask the AI to replace the formula with a shorter one and swap it in once results look similar
Upload the whole workbook with client data so the AI can see the full context of the logic
quiz.x: Explaining the formula and flagging risks (hard-coded values, broken ranges) without exposing data turns days into hours. Uploading the whole workbook (runner-up) adds context but exposes confidential data unnecessarily.

quiz.q: Gemini in Google Sheets proposes a formula for a key figure in a Nigerian company's board pack. The finance director says built-in tools are already verified. How should the analyst treat it?
opts: Accept it if the formula uses standard functions such as SUMIFS or FILTER
Run it twice and accept it if both runs produce the same result in the cell
Apply the same hand-testing and reconciliation used for any other formula
Accept it, as the tool reads the file directly and cannot misread the ranges
quiz.x: The lesson states built-in does not mean verified. Running twice (runner-up) only tests determinism of the formula, not whether its logic is right.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian procurement analyst wants a list that updates automatically showing every invoice above 1,000,000 FCFA for the supplier selected in cell B1. Which function fits best?
opts: XLOOKUP
FILTER
SORT
SUMIFS
quiz.x: FILTER returns a dynamic list of all rows meeting several conditions. XLOOKUP (runner-up) returns a single match, not the full list; SORT only reorders.

facts.t: Searches in any direction and handles not-found values natively.
facts.more: Available in Excel 365 and Google Sheets; keep INDEX/MATCH for older files you must share.

facts.t: Hand-calculate a few rows, including an edge case, to test every new formula.
facts.more: Then reconcile the total to a control figure and trace precedents.

facts.t: Names intermediate calculations inside one Excel formula.
facts.more: Makes long formulas readable and auditable; LAMBDA turns logic into reusable custom functions.

facts.t: Hides every error — including the real ones.
facts.more: Use it narrowly (or IFNA for lookups) so genuine problems still show up.

modules.t: Tool Study: The Finance AI Market
modules.d: Evaluating AI tools for finance by control, accuracy, integration and data protection.
modules.body:
A fast-moving market — evaluate by criteria

Finance AI tools evolve rapidly, and vendors' claims frequently outrun reality. Rather than memorising products, finance leaders need a robust evaluation method. Always confirm current features, pricing, regional availability and data terms with the vendor and through a controlled trial.

Tool categories

  • General AI assistants (for example ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Microsoft Copilot): drafting, explaining, formula help, policy summaries, analysis of documents. Business plans typically offer stronger data protections than consumer plans.
  • Spreadsheet-embedded AI: Copilot in Excel, Gemini in Google Sheets — analysis and formula assistance inside the file.
  • Accounting platforms with AI features: cloud accounting systems (for example QuickBooks, Xero, Sage, Zoho Books) increasingly offer automatic categorisation, bank-matching suggestions and invoice capture.
  • ERP-embedded AI: large systems (for example SAP, Oracle, Microsoft Dynamics) add AI for anomaly detection, forecasting and assistants.
  • Accounts payable and expense automation: invoice capture, three-way matching, approval routing and expense audit.
  • Close management and reconciliation: task tracking, automated matching and variance flagging during month-end.
  • FP&A platforms: planning, forecasting and scenario tools with AI-assisted forecasting and narrative.
  • Audit analytics: full-population testing of transactions for anomalies and unusual patterns.
Local fit matters. For organisations in OHADA member states such as Cameroon, check whether a tool supports the SYSCOHADA chart of accounts and reporting formats, local currency (XAF), French-language interfaces, and local tax requirements — or whether costly customisation would be needed. Many tools built for US or European markets do not do this out of the box.

Evaluation criteria for finance tools

  1. Accuracy: test on your real (anonymised where needed) data — measure error rates, not demo quality.
  2. Control and auditability: are AI suggestions logged? Can you see who approved what? Can outputs be traced to source?
  3. Data protection and residency: where is data stored and processed, is it used to train models, what certifications (such as ISO 27001, SOC 2) does the vendor hold, and is a data-processing agreement available?
  4. Integration: does it connect to your accounting system, bank feeds and spreadsheets without manual exports?
  5. Local compliance: accounting framework (IFRS, SYSCOHADA), tax, e-invoicing and language.
  6. Segregation of duties support: can roles and approvals be configured?
  7. Total cost of ownership: licences, implementation, training, maintenance and change management.
  8. Vendor viability and support: local support, roadmap and exit options for your data.

Running a controlled pilot

Choose one process with measurable pain — for example invoice processing. Establish the baseline: volume, time per invoice, error rate, cycle time. Run the tool in parallel with the existing process for one month, comparing results line by line. Measure accuracy, time saved and exceptions. Only switch over when parallel running shows reliable results and controls are documented. This protects the books from a failed implementation.

Build, buy or configure

Many finance teams can achieve significant gains by configuring what they already own — enabling AI features in existing software, building Power Query and template workflows, and using an approved general assistant — before buying new platforms. Buy when volume, complexity or control requirements justify it. Build custom solutions only with proper IT governance.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my finance systems selection advisor. Ask me about our accounting framework (IFRS or SYSCOHADA), software, transaction volumes, currency, language and pain points. Recommend tool categories to evaluate, build a weighted scoring matrix using the eight criteria in this module, and design a one-month parallel-run pilot with baseline and success measures. List the questions I must ask vendors about data protection and auditability.

📚 Glossary

  • SYSCOHADA: the OHADA accounting system used in member states including Cameroon
  • Data residency: where data is stored and processed geographically
  • Parallel run: operating new and old processes side by side to compare results
  • Three-way match: matching purchase order, goods receipt and invoice before payment
  • SOC 2 / ISO 27001: common information-security assurance standards

📖 References

  • OHADA — Uniform Act on Accounting Law and Financial Reporting (SYSCOHADA revised).
  • IFRS Foundation — IFRS Accounting Standards.
  • AICPA — SOC 2 reports; ISO/IEC 27001.
  • Gartner and vendor documentation — verify current product capabilities.

quiz.q: A vendor demo for invoice capture shows 99% accuracy on sample invoices. A Douala finance manager is interested. What is the best next step?
opts: Compare the vendor's demo accuracy figure with those quoted by two competing vendors
Run a controlled trial on representative anonymised invoices and measure error rates
Negotiate a discount on a three-year licence before the pricing offer expires this month
Ask the vendor for three client references and proceed if they confirm the 99% claim
quiz.x: Accuracy must be tested on your own data, measuring error rates, not demo quality. References (runner-up) help but describe other clients' invoices, not yours.

quiz.q: A Yaoundé company is evaluating a US-built cloud accounting tool with strong AI features. Which local-fit question matters most before shortlisting it?
opts: Does it integrate with the most popular US banks and their real-time payment networks?
Does it offer AI-generated narrative commentary for monthly management packs by default?
Does it have a larger user base in North America than the other tools on the shortlist?
Does it support SYSCOHADA, XAF, French and local tax needs without heavy customisation?
quiz.x: Many US and European tools do not support SYSCOHADA, XAF or local tax out of the box. AI commentary (runner-up) is attractive but irrelevant if the chart of accounts cannot be supported.

quiz.q: A Lagos company's external auditor asks which tool feature will matter most for relying on AI-assisted processing next year. Which criterion is most directly relevant?
opts: Logged suggestions and approvals traceable to source
Faster processing time per invoice at month-end
Higher accuracy rates on demo invoice samples
Integration with the team's existing spreadsheets
quiz.x: Auditability — logs, approvals and traceability — is what lets auditors rely on the process. Accuracy (runner-up) matters, but auditors still need evidence of who approved what.

quiz.q: A Kenyan finance team wants to switch its invoice process to a new AI tool starting at the next month-end close. What is the best rollout approach?
opts: Switch fully and keep the old system's data accessible in case staff need to look things up
Switch at month-end but have a senior accountant review every invoice for the first week
Run the tool in parallel with the current process and compare results before switching
Switch mid-month when volumes are lower, then extend to the full close once it stabilises
quiz.x: A parallel run produces evidence the new process works before it is relied on. Switching mid-month with review (runner-up) lowers pressure but gives no side-by-side comparison.

quiz.q: Before uploading supplier invoices containing bank details to an AI tool, a Ghanaian CFO prepares vendor questions. Which matters most for data protection?
opts: How quickly can the tool process invoices during month-end peaks in transaction volume?
Where is data stored and processed, is it used for training, and is a DPA available?
Does the vendor offer local training sessions for staff during the implementation?
Can the tool read invoices in both English and French, including handwritten scans?
quiz.x: Storage location, training use and a data-processing agreement are the core data protection questions. Language support (runner-up) is a valid local-fit question but not about data protection.

quiz.q: A five-person finance team in Kigali has Microsoft 365 and a cloud accounting system whose AI features are switched off. Budget is tight. What is the most sensible first move?
opts: Let each team member choose a free AI tool so the team learns what works best for them
Wait for the vendor's next major release before using any of the AI features at all
Buy a specialist AP automation tool, since invoice processing is the largest workload
Configure the existing AI features and build templates before buying anything new
quiz.x: Using capabilities already paid for, with templates and controls, is the low-cost start. A specialist AP tool (runner-up) may come later once baseline needs and data are clear.

quiz.q: A US distributor is piloting invoice automation. Which baseline should be captured before the pilot to judge its success fairly?
opts: Number of invoices exceeding the approval threshold
The licence cost compared with current staff salaries
Volume, time per invoice, error rate and cycle time
Staff satisfaction with the current invoice process
quiz.x: A baseline of volume, time, errors and cycle time allows before/after comparison. Licence versus salary cost (runner-up) is a cost view, not a measure of process performance.

quiz.q: An AP tool being configured at a Nairobi firm allows one user role to capture, approve and release payment for an invoice. Which control concern does this raise?
opts: Segregation of duties
Change management
Exception handling
Model risk management
quiz.x: One person initiating, approving and paying breaches segregation of duties. Exception handling (runner-up) concerns routing unusual items, not who holds which rights.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian group's business case lists only licence fees for a close-management tool. Why should total cost of ownership also include change management?
opts: Training and process redesign often cost as much as, or more than, the licences
Auditors require change management costs to be capitalised alongside the licence
Change management costs are tax-deductible and therefore improve the business case
Licence fees for finance tools are usually waived during the first contract year
quiz.x: Training, process redesign and adoption effort are frequently as large as licence costs. The tax-deductibility point (runner-up) is irrelevant to whether costs belong in TCO.

quiz.q: A vendor tells a South African CFO it holds a SOC 2 report. What does this mainly give the CFO?
opts: A legal commitment that client data will be stored in South Africa
Certification that the tool complies with IFRS and local tax rules
Independent assurance on the vendor's security and related controls
Confirmation that the tool's AI outputs are accurate for finance use
quiz.x: SOC 2 is an independent report on security-related controls. It says nothing about AI output accuracy (runner-up), which still needs your own trial.

facts.t: Recommended parallel run before switching a finance process to a new tool.
facts.more: Compare line by line with the existing process; switch only when results and controls are proven.

facts.t: An independent attestation of a service provider's security controls.
facts.more: Ask for it, or ISO/IEC 27001 certification, plus a data-processing agreement, before sending finance data.

facts.t: Currency code a Cameroon-ready tool must support, alongside SYSCOHADA and French.
facts.more: Many US- or Europe-built tools need costly customisation for OHADA reporting.

facts.t: Total cost of ownership: licences, implementation, training, maintenance, change.
facts.more: The licence is often the smaller part of the true cost.

modules.d: Variance analysis, driver-based forecasting, scenarios and commentary that leaders actually use.
modules.body:
From numbers to decisions

Financial planning and analysis exists to help leaders make better decisions: where to invest, what to cut, how to price, and what risks lie ahead. The value is not in the spreadsheet but in the insight and how clearly it is communicated. AI accelerates the mechanics and drafting so analysts can spend more time understanding causes and advising.

Variance analysis that explains, not just reports

A variance tells you what changed; analysis tells you why. Break revenue and cost variances into drivers. For sales: price variance = (actual price − budget price) × actual quantity; volume variance = (actual quantity − budget quantity) × budget price. Together they reconcile to the total revenue variance. Similar logic applies to costs (rate and usage variances). Then investigate causes: a negative volume variance might come from a lost client, delayed product launch or seasonal shift. Good commentary states the variance, the driver, the cause, whether it is timing or permanent, and the action.

Worked example. Budget: 1,000 units at 5,000 FCFA = 5,000,000. Actual: 900 units at 5,400 FCFA = 4,860,000. Total variance −140,000. Price variance = (5,400 − 5,000) × 900 = +360,000 favourable. Volume variance = (900 − 1,000) × 5,000 = −500,000 adverse. Commentary: "Revenue was 140,000 FCFA below budget. An 8% price increase added 360,000, but volume fell 10%, costing 500,000, mainly due to the loss of Distributor X in May. We expect volume to recover partially from Q3 with two new distributors."

Driver-based forecasting

Instead of forecasting each line from last year plus a percentage, driver-based models link outcomes to operational drivers: number of customers × average order value × purchase frequency; headcount × average cost; units produced × cost per unit. Changing a driver updates the forecast consistently. AI can help identify plausible drivers, structure the model and write formulas — while finance and operations agree the assumptions.

Rolling forecasts and scenarios

A rolling forecast always looks a fixed period ahead (for example 12 or 18 months), updated monthly or quarterly, rather than stopping at year-end. Scenario analysis tests base, upside and downside cases with explicitly different assumptions — for example a currency movement, a loss of a major customer or a fuel price rise. Sensitivity analysis changes one variable at a time to show which assumptions matter most. AI is useful for generating a structured list of plausible scenarios and drafting the narrative of their implications, but the quantification must be in the model.

Key ratios and what they reveal

  • Profitability: gross margin, operating margin, net margin, return on capital.
  • Liquidity: current ratio, quick ratio, cash conversion cycle (DSO + DIO − DPO).
  • Efficiency: asset turnover, inventory days, receivable days.
  • Leverage: debt-to-equity, interest cover.

Ratios are meaningful only in context — trends over time, comparison with budget and with peers — and alongside understanding of the business.

Writing commentary leaders use

Executives want the answer first. Structure commentary as: headline (the key message), the two or three most important drivers, risks and opportunities ahead, and recommended actions or decisions needed. Avoid listing every variance; focus on what is material. AI can draft commentary from your verified analysis, adapt it for different audiences — board, operations managers, donors, lenders — and check clarity. You remain responsible for every number and claim.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my FP&A partner. I will give you budget and actual figures for price, volume and costs (non-confidential or anonymised). Build the formulas to split the variance into price and volume (and rate and usage for costs), check that they reconcile, and draft a one-paragraph management commentary leading with the headline. Then propose base, upside and downside scenarios with the key assumptions to model, and identify the two most sensitive drivers.

📚 Glossary

  • Price / volume variance: splitting revenue variance into price and quantity effects
  • Driver-based forecast: forecast built from operational drivers
  • Rolling forecast: forecast that always extends a fixed period ahead
  • Sensitivity analysis: changing one assumption to see its effect
  • Cash conversion cycle: DSO + DIO − DPO

📖 References

  • CIMA — Management accounting and variance analysis resources.
  • AFP — FP&A guides and best practices.
  • Minto, B. The Pyramid Principle — for commentary structure.

quiz.q: A Douala beverage firm budgeted 2,000 cases at 3,000 FCFA. It sold 2,200 cases at 2,800 FCFA. What is the sales volume variance?
opts: +160,000 FCFA favourable
−440,000 FCFA adverse
+560,000 FCFA favourable
+600,000 FCFA favourable
quiz.x: Volume variance = (2,200 − 2,000) × budget price 3,000 = +600,000. Using actual price gives 560,000 (runner-up), which mixes price into the volume effect.

quiz.q: Using the same data (budget 2,000 cases at 3,000 FCFA; actual 2,200 at 2,800 FCFA), what is the price variance?
opts: +160,000 FCFA favourable
−440,000 FCFA adverse
+600,000 FCFA favourable
−400,000 FCFA adverse
quiz.x: Price variance = (2,800 − 3,000) × actual quantity 2,200 = −440,000. Using budget quantity gives −400,000 (runner-up); with actual quantity the two variances reconcile to the +160,000 total.

quiz.q: A Ghanaian CEO has ten minutes before a board meeting and asks for the monthly commentary. Which structure serves her best?
opts: Headline, two or three key drivers with causes, outlook and actions needed
The full variance table with AI-generated comments added to each line
A chronological narrative of the month's events, ending with the result
Every variance above 1% listed by cost centre, with a cause for each line
quiz.x: Executives want the answer first and the material drivers. Listing every variance (runner-up) is thorough but buries the message the CEO needs.

quiz.q: A Kenyan logistics company forecasts each cost line as last year plus 5%. Fuel use depends on kilometres driven, which will rise 20%. What is the main weakness of its method?
opts: Last year's figures may include one-off costs that will not be repeated
Costs are not linked to the operational drivers that actually move them
The forecast is prepared once a year rather than on a rolling basis
A 5% uplift is too low for an economy with inflation above that level
quiz.x: Driver-based forecasting links costs to drivers such as kilometres, so a 20% rise flows through. One-off costs (runner-up) are a valid concern but not the structural weakness the scenario shows.

quiz.q: In October, a Nigerian manufacturer's CFO wants a forecast that still looks 12 months ahead next March. What best describes this, compared with an annual budget?
opts: A sensitivity analysis changing one assumption each month to the year-end
A rolling budget that is set once a year and then frozen for performance targets
A rolling forecast extending a fixed period ahead, updated each month or quarter
A scenario forecast with base, upside and downside cases for the calendar year
quiz.x: A rolling forecast keeps a fixed horizon rather than stopping at year-end. Scenario forecasting (runner-up) tests alternative cases but can still stop at year-end.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian importer's analyst asks AI to estimate the profit impact of a 15% depreciation in the currency against the US dollar. What is the best approach?
opts: Ask AI to compute the impact under three different exchange rates and average them
Ask AI for the profit impact, then compare it with the impact from the last shock
Apply 15% to total costs in the model and ask AI to write the board commentary
Use AI to list affected lines and assumptions, then quantify the case in the model
quiz.x: AI helps structure scenarios; the quantification belongs in the model. Applying 15% to total costs (runner-up) uses the model but wrongly assumes every cost is dollar-linked.

quiz.q: A Kampala distributor reports DSO of 52 days, DIO of 38 days and DPO of 41 days. What is its cash conversion cycle?
opts: 49 days
55 days
131 days
27 days
quiz.x: CCC = DSO + DIO − DPO = 52 + 38 − 41 = 49 days. Subtracting DIO instead (52 − 38 + 41 = 55) is the likely runner-up error.

quiz.q: Revenue at an Abidjan firm is below June budget solely because a large order shipped on 2 July instead of 29 June. How should the commentary classify this?
opts: A price variance from a delayed shipment
A permanent revenue loss requiring a reforecast now
A volume variance caused by weaker demand
A timing variance expected to reverse in July
quiz.x: The order was delayed, not lost, so it is timing and should reverse. Calling it a volume variance (runner-up) is technically where it appears but misstates the cause and outlook.

quiz.q: A US SaaS company's forecast relies on churn, price, new customers and salary growth. The CFO wants to know which assumption the result is most sensitive to. Which analysis fits?
opts: Variance analysis comparing actual with budget
Ratio analysis over the past three fiscal years
Sensitivity analysis changing one variable at a time
Scenario analysis combining several assumptions at once
quiz.x: Sensitivity analysis isolates each variable's effect. Scenario analysis (runner-up) moves several assumptions together, so it cannot show which single one matters most.

quiz.q: AI drafts board commentary for a Rwandan firm stating that margin improved due to stronger supplier negotiations. The analyst has not confirmed any cause. What should she do?
opts: Keep it, since supplier negotiations are the most common cause of margin gains
Verify the cause with procurement, or remove it, before the pack is submitted
Keep it but soften it to 'likely' so the board knows it is an interpretation
Ask the AI for supporting evidence and keep the claim if it provides a reason
quiz.x: The analyst is responsible for every claim, so an unverified cause must be confirmed or removed. Softening to 'likely' (runner-up) still presents an untested cause to the board.

facts.t: Cash conversion cycle: days cash is tied up in operations.
facts.more: Days sales outstanding plus inventory days minus payables days. Shorter usually means less financing needed.

facts.t: Worked example: +360,000 price variance and −500,000 volume variance.
facts.more: Price and volume variances together reconcile to the total revenue variance.

facts.t: Typical horizon of a rolling forecast, updated monthly or quarterly.
facts.more: It always looks the same distance ahead instead of stopping at year-end.

facts.t: Executives want the headline before the detail.
facts.more: Headline, two or three drivers, risks and opportunities, then the decision needed.

270,000 above budget.

while 10% higher volume added 600,000.

Volume variance uses the budget price: (2,200 − 2,000) × 3,000.
The discount won the new Kribi distributor,
which guarantees volume growth for the next five years.
Overclaim — no forecast is guaranteed; state as expected, with assumptions.
We recommend reviewing discount terms at the Q3 forecast.

modules.d: Keeping AI-assisted finance reliable, auditable and compliant with IFRS, SYSCOHADA and internal control frameworks.
modules.body:
Why controls matter more, not less, with AI

Internal controls exist to provide reasonable assurance that financial reporting is reliable, operations effective and laws respected. AI changes how work is done — and therefore where errors and fraud can occur. A team that adopts AI without redesigning controls is quietly increasing its risk.

The COSO internal control framework

The COSO framework, widely used worldwide, has five components: control environment (tone at the top, integrity, accountability), risk assessment (identifying risks to objectives, including fraud and change risks), control activities (approvals, reconciliations, segregation of duties, system controls), information and communication (quality information flowing to the right people), and monitoring activities (ongoing and periodic evaluation). Introducing AI should trigger a risk assessment: what new risks does this process change create, and which controls address them?

Key controls for AI-assisted finance

  • Maker–checker review: AI-assisted work (journals, reconciliations, reports) is prepared by one person and reviewed by another with evidence of review.
  • Segregation of duties: no single person (or automated workflow they control) can initiate, approve and record a transaction.
  • Reconciliation to independent sources: AI-produced figures reconcile to the ledger, bank statements or sub-ledgers.
  • Logging and documentation: prompts, tool versions, inputs and outputs for significant processes are retained where practical; methods are documented.
  • Access controls: only authorised staff use approved tools with financial data; data rules define what may be entered.
  • Change management: changes to automated workflows, models or AI configurations are approved, tested and recorded.
  • Exception handling: automated processes route unusual items to human review rather than processing them silently.
Model risk. Any model used for decisions — a forecast, an expected credit loss model, an AI classifier for expenses — can be wrong. Model risk management means documenting the model's purpose, assumptions and limitations, validating it independently, monitoring performance over time, and having a human owner accountable for it.

Accounting frameworks and AI

AI can summarise and explain standards, but accounting judgements must rely on the authoritative text and qualified professionals. In OHADA member states such as Cameroon, entities apply the SYSCOHADA system under the OHADA Uniform Act on accounting (revised version in force since 2018), with IFRS required for certain entities such as those listed or issuing public securities. Elsewhere, IFRS or national standards apply. An AI answer about revenue recognition, leases or provisions is a starting point for research, never the final authority. Always cite the specific standard and paragraph in working papers.

Confidentiality and data protection

Finance handles payroll, customer financial data, banking details and unpublished results. Apply clear rules: personal and confidential financial data only in approved tools with appropriate contractual protections; no unpublished price-sensitive information in public tools; anonymise where analysis does not require identities. Comply with applicable data protection law and professional confidentiality duties.

Fraud and AI

AI cuts both ways. It helps detect fraud through full-population analytics — duplicate payments, round-amount patterns, unusual timing, vendors sharing bank details with employees. But criminals also use AI: convincing phishing emails, fake invoices and voice or video impersonation of executives requesting urgent transfers. Controls must include independent verification of payment instructions through a known channel, especially for changes to supplier bank details and urgent requests from "senior executives".

Professional ethics

Professional bodies' codes — such as the IESBA Code of Ethics — require integrity, objectivity, professional competence and due care, confidentiality and professional behaviour. Using AI does not reduce these duties: the professional remains responsible for the work signed.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my internal control advisor. I will describe a finance process where we use or plan to use AI. Map the process steps, identify the new risks AI introduces, and map controls to the five COSO components. Recommend specific maker-checker, segregation, reconciliation, logging and exception-handling controls, and draft a short control description suitable for audit documentation.

📚 Glossary

  • COSO: framework of five internal control components
  • Maker–checker: preparation by one person, review by another
  • Segregation of duties: separating initiation, approval, recording and custody
  • Model risk: risk of loss from incorrect or misused models
  • Business email compromise: fraud using impersonated emails to divert payments

📖 References

  • COSO (2013). Internal Control — Integrated Framework.
  • OHADA — Uniform Act on Accounting Law and Financial Reporting (revised 2017, applicable from 2018).
  • IFRS Foundation — IFRS Accounting Standards.
  • IESBA — International Code of Ethics for Professional Accountants.
  • ACFE — Fraud examination resources.

quiz.q: At a Douala firm, an accountant can generate AI-suggested journals and post them directly to the ledger with no second person involved. Which control is most clearly missing?
opts: Change management
Model validation work
Access controls
Maker–checker review
quiz.x: Preparation and posting by one person without review lacks maker–checker. Access controls (runner-up) limit who uses tools but do not add independent review of each journal.

quiz.q: A Nairobi company plans to introduce an AI expense-classification tool. Under COSO, which activity should come first?
opts: Updating the code of conduct for staff
Monitoring the tool's accuracy over time
A risk assessment of the changed process
Communicating the change to all budget holders
quiz.x: A process change should trigger risk assessment to identify new risks and needed controls. Monitoring (runner-up) is important but follows once controls are designed and running.

quiz.q: An AP clerk in Accra receives an email, apparently from the CEO, with new supplier bank details and an urgent request to pay today. The email looks genuine. What should she do?
opts: Verify the change with the supplier and CEO through a known channel before paying
Reply to the email asking the CEO to confirm the new details in writing before paying
Pay a small portion today and hold the balance until the supplier confirms receipt
Run the email through an AI tool that checks whether the writing style is the CEO's
quiz.x: Independent verification via a known channel defeats business email compromise. Replying to the email (runner-up) goes back to the possibly compromised sender.

quiz.q: An AI model at a US firm classifies expenses with 96% accuracy and is now used for VAT reclaim. Who should be accountable for the model's performance?
opts: The software vendor that supplied the AI model
A named human model owner inside the organisation
The external auditor who tests the VAT reclaims
The AP clerks whose expense coding it replaced
quiz.x: Model risk management requires a named, accountable human owner. The vendor (runner-up) supplies the model but cannot own the organisation's risk.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian accountant asks AI how to treat a complex lease and records the entries based on its answer. What is missing?
opts: A second AI tool's answer to confirm the treatment before the entries are recorded
Checking the authoritative standard text and, where needed, a qualified professional
An explanation of the treatment in the journal description field for the auditors
Approval from the line manager that the lease treatment looks reasonable to them
quiz.x: AI answers are a starting point; the authoritative standard and qualified judgement are required. A second AI (runner-up) adds no authority and can share the same errors.

quiz.q: Which Cameroonian entity would most likely be required to apply IFRS in addition to SYSCOHADA under the revised OHADA Uniform Act?
opts: A family-owned SME with turnover above 1 billion FCFA
A subsidiary of a French group reporting to Paris
An NGO receiving grants from international donors
A company whose shares are listed on a stock exchange
quiz.x: The lesson notes IFRS is required for entities that are listed or issue public securities. A foreign subsidiary (runner-up) may prepare IFRS packs for its parent, but that is a group requirement, not the Uniform Act rule.

quiz.q: An AI reconciliation tool at a Lagos bank auto-matches transactions. Some unusual items are matched without anyone seeing them. Which control best addresses this?
opts: Exception handling routing unusual items to review
A monthly summary report of all matched totals by account
Annual revalidation of the matching model
Segregation of the matching and posting roles
quiz.x: Exception handling sends unusual items to humans rather than processing them silently. Segregation (runner-up) is good practice but would not surface the unusual items.

quiz.q: A full-population test at a Kigali hospital finds that an employee's personal bank account matches a supplier's bank details. What is this an example of?
opts: A segregation of duties failure in the AP process
Proof that the employee committed procurement fraud
Analytics flagging a fraud red flag for follow-up
An error in master data that should be auto-corrected
quiz.x: A matching account is a red flag requiring investigation, not proof. Calling it proof of fraud (runner-up) skips the investigation the evidence still needs.

quiz.q: A Ghanaian team edits the prompt and settings of its automated bank reconciliation workflow to fix an issue, without testing or approval. Which control has failed?
opts: Maker–checker review
Prompt logs
Exception handling
Change management
quiz.x: Changes to automated workflows must be approved, tested and recorded. Logging (runner-up) may record that a change occurred but does not require testing or approval.

quiz.q: A Kenyan chartered accountant signs financial statements prepared with heavy AI assistance. Under the IESBA Code, who is responsible for their accuracy?
opts: Shared equally by the accountant and the vendor
The vendor of the AI tool used to prepare them
The professional accountant who signs them
The junior staff who wrote the prompts used
quiz.x: Ethics codes leave responsibility with the signing professional; AI does not reduce due care. Junior staff (runner-up) contribute but do not carry the signing professional's duty.

facts.t: COSO 2013: five components of internal control, supported by 17 principles.
facts.more: Control environment, risk assessment, control activities, information and communication, monitoring.

facts.t: Year the revised SYSCOHADA accounting system came into force.
facts.more: Under the revised OHADA Uniform Act on accounting; IFRS applies to certain entities such as listed issuers.

facts.t: Share of leading digits that are '1' in many natural financial datasets (Benford's law).
facts.more: Auditors use deviations from this pattern as one signal of possible manipulation — a prompt to investigate, not proof.

facts.t: One prepares, another reviews with evidence.
facts.more: AI-assisted journals and reconciliations still need an independent reviewer.

plaibox.intro: You are chief accountant at a Yaoundé NGO using AI in the close. The auditors arrive.
plaibox.win: Strong control thinking — traceability, authoritative sources and segregation of duties held up.
plaibox.lose: Review COSO and the key controls for AI-assisted finance, then retry.

modules.t: Capstone: Your Finance AI Workflow File
modules.d: Design, document and test one AI-assisted finance workflow to audit-ready standard.
modules.body:
The goal: one workflow, done properly

Rather than collecting tips, you will redesign one real finance workflow from your own work using AI — and document it so that a colleague can run it and an auditor can rely on it. Typical choices: monthly variance commentary, bank reconciliation preparation, supplier invoice coding, cash flow forecast update, expense review, or a management pack.

The workflow file structure

  1. Process overview: purpose, frequency, owner, inputs, outputs and users of the output.
  2. Before-and-after map: the current steps with time per step, and the redesigned steps showing where AI is used.
  3. Calculation boundary: which steps use deterministic tools (formulas, Power Query, accounting system) and which use AI for drafting, explanation or checking.
  4. Prompt library: the exact prompts used, with input templates and expected output format.
  5. Data rules: what data is used, classification, the approved tool and anonymisation steps.
  6. Controls: maker–checker review, reconciliations to control figures, exception handling, and evidence retained.
  7. Testing record: results of at least one parallel run comparing the new workflow with the old.
  8. Benefits measurement: time saved, error rate, cycle time, and quality feedback from users.
  9. Risks and limitations: what could go wrong and how it is mitigated.
  10. Maintenance: who updates the workflow and when it is reviewed.
The colleague test. Give your workflow file to a colleague who has never done the process. If they can produce the correct output, with the same controls, using only the file, your documentation is good enough. If they need to ask you questions, improve the file.

Measuring and presenting the benefit

Quantify the baseline and new performance. For example: "Monthly variance commentary previously took 9 hours over 3 days; the redesigned workflow takes 3.5 hours in 1 day, with commentary rated clearer by the management team, and no reconciliation errors in two parallel runs." Translate time saved into value: what higher-value work will the team do with the freed time?

Scaling responsibly

Once one workflow is proven, use the same file structure for the next. A finance team that builds five well-documented workflows over a year has transformed its operations with controls intact — far more valuable than widespread, undocumented use.

Your capstone deliverable

Submit the completed workflow file, the evidence from one parallel run, and a one-page summary for your finance leader with the benefits, controls and recommendation. Your mentor reviews it for accuracy, control quality and practicality.

🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as my finance workflow designer. I will describe one recurring finance process. Help me build the full workflow file: process overview, before-and-after map with time estimates, calculation boundary, exact prompts with input templates, data classification, controls with evidence, a parallel-run test plan, benefit measures, risks and maintenance. Then review the file as an external auditor and list any gaps.

Going deeper — capstone playbook: your Finance AI Workflow File

This capstone is about audit-readiness. A reviewer should be able to pick up your file, rerun the workflow and reach the same numbers, see exactly where AI touched the process, and find the evidence that every AI output was checked against control figures.

Step-by-step timeline.

  • Week 1 — Baseline. Choose the workflow, map current steps with timings, collect one period's inputs and outputs, and note errors or rework from recent cycles.
  • Week 2 — Redesign. Define the calculation boundary (deterministic tools for numbers, AI for drafting, explanation and checking), write the prompt library and data rules, and design maker–checker controls.
  • Week 3 — Parallel run. Run old and new workflows on the same period; reconcile every figure; log differences, root causes and time taken.
  • Week 4 — Document and present. Complete the workflow file, pass the colleague test and present the benefits with evidence.

Deliverables checklist.

  • ☐ Workflow file (all sections listed above)
  • ☐ Before-and-after process map with timings
  • ☐ Prompt library with input templates
  • ☐ Control matrix and evidence samples
  • ☐ Parallel-run reconciliation
  • ☐ Benefits and risk summary

Assessment rubric (weighted).

  • Control and audit trail — 30%: maker–checker, reconciliations and evidence retained
  • Calculation integrity — 20%: numbers produced deterministically and tie to source
  • Documentation quality — 20%: passes the colleague test
  • Measured benefit — 15%: credible baseline and results
  • Data protection and compliance — 15%: classification, approved tools, relevant standards such as IFRS or SYSCOHADA
Worked mini-example. An accountant at a Yaoundé distribution company redesigns monthly variance commentary. Variances are computed in the spreadsheet from the trial balance; only the variance table (no customer names) goes to an approved AI tool, with a prompt that requests commentary citing each figure. The checker ticks every number in the draft back to the table; in the parallel run, the AI attributed one variance to "price increases" when the ledger showed a reclassification, which the checker corrected. The workflow file adds a rule: explanations must come from preparer notes, not AI inference.

Common failure modes.

  • Letting AI perform calculations that must be exact.
  • No parallel run, so errors are discovered after reporting.
  • Prompts stored in someone's chat history instead of the file.
  • Uploading unanonymised ledger or payroll data to unapproved tools.
  • Claiming time savings without a measured baseline.

Submission and presentation structure.

  • 1. Workflow purpose and baseline pain
  • 2. Redesign and calculation boundary
  • 3. Controls and parallel-run evidence
  • 4. Benefits measured
  • 5. Risks, maintenance and next workflow
🧪 Interactive Lab — try it now

Act as an external auditor reviewing my AI-assisted finance workflow. Here is my workflow file summary and control matrix: [paste, anonymised]. Identify where an AI error could reach the final output undetected, test whether my calculation boundary is clear, and list the evidence you would request to rely on this workflow. Suggest the minimum additional controls needed.

📚 Glossary

  • Workflow file: complete documentation of a redesigned process
  • Parallel run: running old and new processes side by side to compare
  • Colleague test: checking that someone else can run the process from the documentation
  • Control figure: independent total used to verify output

📖 References

  • COSO (2013). Internal Control — Integrated Framework.
  • ICAEW — Generative AI guidance.
  • Team21 Academy, AI Unlocked workflow templates.

quiz.q: A Yaoundé finance officer is choosing a capstone workflow. Which choice best fits the module's brief?
opts: Collecting twenty useful AI prompts that different colleagues use for finance tasks
Redesigning monthly variance commentary with prompts, controls and a parallel run
Writing an AI policy for the whole finance department covering all permitted uses
Testing five AI tools on the same reconciliation to choose the best for the team
quiz.x: The capstone redesigns one real workflow end to end and documents it. A prompt collection (runner-up) is the 'collecting tips' approach the module explicitly moves away from.

quiz.q: In a Nairobi team's variance-commentary workflow file, which step belongs in a deterministic tool rather than an AI assistant?
opts: Calculating price and volume variances
Drafting the headline of the commentary
Suggesting likely causes to investigate
Adapting the text for different readers
quiz.x: Calculations stay in formulas or the accounting system. Suggesting causes (runner-up) is a legitimate AI task as long as the analyst verifies them.

quiz.q: A colleague in Douala tries to run the bank reconciliation using only the workflow file but has to ask the author several questions. What should happen?
opts: Record a video walkthrough to accompany the existing workflow file
Improve the file until a colleague can complete it independently
Accept it, since some questions are normal for a complex process
Add the author's phone number to the file for future questions
quiz.x: The colleague test is passed when the file alone suffices. A video (runner-up) may help but does not fix gaps in the documented steps and controls.

quiz.q: A Lagos finance team includes a parallel-run testing record in its workflow file. What is its main purpose?
opts: Training material for new staff who will run the workflow in future
Proof to the vendor that the AI tool has been used for its full trial
A record of time saved to include in the benefits measurement section
Evidence the new workflow gives correct results before it is relied on
quiz.x: A parallel run evidences correctness before reliance. Time saved (runner-up) can be captured during it, but correctness is the purpose.

quiz.q: A Cameroonian analyst is drafting the benefits section of her workflow file. Which statement is most credible to a finance leader?
opts: Commentary is now 61% faster and AI is expected to save around 70 hours over the next year
AI has transformed our commentary process and the whole team now works much more efficiently
Commentary time fell from 9 to 3.5 hours, with no reconciliation errors in two parallel runs
Management feedback on the new commentary has been very positive and the team is motivated
quiz.x: A baseline-to-new measure with quality evidence is credible. The 61% claim (runner-up) is precise but projects savings without showing error-free evidence.

quiz.q: A Kampala reviewer wants to know whether payroll data may be pasted into the team's general assistant. Which section of the workflow file should answer this?
opts: Data rules
Process overview
Prompt library
Controls
quiz.x: Data rules set classification, approved tools and anonymisation. Controls (runner-up) cover review and reconciliation, not what data enters which tool.

quiz.q: A Ghanaian finance team has proven its first documented workflow. What does the course recommend next?
opts: Reuse the same file structure for the next workflow, building a documented set
Ask each team member to design their own workflow format for their own process
Spend a year refining the first workflow before attempting a second one at all
Roll AI use out across all processes quickly while the team's enthusiasm is high
quiz.x: Scaling with a consistent file structure keeps controls intact. A fast rollout (runner-up) risks the widespread undocumented use the module warns against.

quiz.q: A US company's controller asks what evidence to keep from an audited AI-assisted reconciliation. Which is most valuable?
opts: The analyst's notes on how long each step took
The full chat history of every AI conversation used in preparing it
A screenshot of the AI tool's settings for each month
Reviewer sign-off and reconciliation to the control figure
quiz.x: Review evidence and reconciliation to a control figure are what auditors rely on. Full chat history (runner-up) can support logging but does not prove the result was checked.

quiz.q: A Rwandan finance team is finalising its workflow file and must fill in the maintenance section. Who should be named there?
opts: Every team member, so that nobody is a single point of failure
The external auditor, who reviews the process each year
A responsible owner who reviews and updates it on a schedule
The AI vendor's account manager who supports the tool used
quiz.x: Maintenance needs one accountable owner and a review cycle. Naming everyone (runner-up) sounds resilient but leaves no one clearly accountable.

quiz.q: A redesigned Nigerian workflow saves time but creates a risk that confidential payroll data enters a general AI tool. What should the file include?
opts: A note telling staff to be careful with payroll data when they use the general tool
A mitigation such as anonymisation or an approved protected tool, in the risk section
A plan to drop the time savings and return to the old process for payroll months
A reference to the IT security policy, which already covers data in all AI tools
quiz.x: Risks must be documented with concrete mitigations. A generic 'be careful' note (runner-up) states the risk without an effective control.
